facts.text: The opening walk along the railroad tracks was shot in downtown Los Angeles without a permit. Guerrilla filmmaking, 1987 style.
Creepozoids was originally titled "Mutant Spawn 2000." DeCoteau meant to save "Creepozoids" for another project, but Charles Band loved it so much he told him to use it here.
Director David DeCoteau said it was shot in 15 days in a Los Angeles warehouse. It was his first feature shot on 35mm film.
Budget reports vary wildly. DeCoteau recalled about $150K, while TMDB lists just $75,000. Either way, that's a lot of slime per dollar.
The set was the abandoned studio of Hustler photographer Suze Randall, on Washington Blvd. in Marina del Rey.
Kim McKamy was first cast as Blanca and Linnea Quigley as Kate. McKamy balked at the nudity and Quigley said she was fine with it, so they swapped roles.
Kim McKamy soon began a career in adult films as Ashlyn Gere. She later landed a regular role on TV's Space: Above and Beyond.
For the shower scene, a water jug was rigged overhead. Production designer Royce Mathew reportedly used exactly 4.5 gallons from a drinking-cooler bottle, in a one-take setup.
Linnea Quigley pranked co-star Ken Abraham after this scene. He'd been working out at 5 a.m. to prep, so she told him they had to reshoot it. He started doing push-ups.
Linnea Quigley's feet were so small the production had to buy child-size boots for her.
Writer Dave Eisenstark, credited as "Burford Hauser," got the story from DeCoteau in about 30 minutes. He then had seven days to deliver the script.
While watching dailies, Charles Band held up ten fingers at DeCoteau. It meant a ten-picture deal. They drew up a contract and opened a $100 bottle of Dom Perignon.
Peter Carsillo designed the main monster. Thomas Floutz built the suit and also performed inside it.
The film is set in 1998, six years after a nuclear war. Its poster tagline: "Your flesh will crawl right off your bones!"
Ashlyn Gere's fight with Linnea Quigley was partly done by a stunt woman in prosthetic make-up doubling for Gere.
Quigley said in Fangoria that the script had more sex scenes involving her and the monster. Her character was to be impregnated by it.
Employee file #213483 lists names from the Empire crowd: Forrest J Ackerman, Roger Corman, Charles Band and David DeCoteau (as David McCabe).
This was the first film Linnea Quigley produced. She was also credited as associate producer.
Production designer Royce Mathew reportedly worked 18 hours a day, seven days a week. He built the creature's lair overnight, finishing as the crew arrived.
Psychotronic Video's Michael Weldon called the creature effects "pretty bad." TV Guide gave it 1 star out of 4 and called it an Alien imitation.
It ran theatrically as a double bill with Slave Girls from Beyond Infinity (1987). It became a hit on video.
Joe Bob's Drive-In Theater aired Creepozoids on October 3, 1992.
A sequel was planned in 1988 but fell through on rights issues after Empire Pictures collapsed.
Fred Olen Ray remade it as Hybrid in 1997.
On the Blu-ray commentary, DeCoteau says "Boom!" so often that a drinking game would have you passed out before the end credits.
